subject.title: skill safe-encryption-skill: Spec Prohibits File Output But CLI Tool's Standard Interface Is File Output

question: Should ClawHub require a corrected publisher release first, or place a moderation hold on the current safe-encryption-skill version until its contradictory encryption-output guidance is corrected?
rationale: The package is publisher-owned, and selecting between a correction window and a registry restriction sets the project’s security-moderation threshold rather than a mechanical repository change.

options.title: Require a corrected package release
options.body: Ask the publisher to clarify final-output versus intermediate-file handling and add an explicit encryption pipe example, then re-review the new version.

options.title: Hold the current version pending correction
options.body: Apply the available moderation restriction if maintainers judge the contradictory handling guidance unsafe enough to block new installs now.

options.title: Document-only follow-up
options.body: Leave the current version available and record guidance for future package reviews, accepting continued ambiguity for existing users.

recommendation.title: Require a corrected package release
recommendation.body: Ask the publisher to clarify final-output versus intermediate-file handling and add an explicit encryption pipe example, then re-review the new version.

likelyOwner.reason: A corrected published package version is the primary remediation path; registry staff can apply any resulting moderation decision.
